L1, any use disorder (DSM-5 ≥ 2 criteria); L2, moderate-to-severe use disorder (DSM-5 ≥ 4) or dependence; † dependence scale (KDS ≥ 14, SDS or LDQ at the authors' cut-off); ‡ ASSIST ≥ 27; L3, severe use disorder (DSM-5 ≥ 6). Leong Bin Abdullah (2019) reported only KDS ≥ 35 beside a merged 0–34 band (43/150, 28.7%), which fits no level; it is described but not pooled. JBI items: 2, participants sampled appropriately; 6, valid methods for identifying the condition; 9, adequate response rate (Y, yes; N, no; U, unclear). ASSIST, Alcohol, Smoking and Substance Involvement Screening Test; DSM-5-SUD, DSM-5 substance use disorder checklist; KDS, Kratom Dependence Scale; LDQ, Leeds Dependence Questionnaire; SDS, Severity of Dependence Scale; SUDST, Substance Use Disorder Screening Test (DSM-5 checklist); NR, not reported.

Binomial–normal generalized linear mixed models with a logit link. The Southeast Asia model did not converge in metafor and was fitted with lme4 (Wald CI; prediction interval from τ). PI, prediction interval. All sensitivity analyses: Table S1.

The multilevel model nests estimates (L1, L2, L3) within samples (binomial GLMM, lme4, Wald CI). Regular use required: the sample was restricted to people using kratom at least weekly or daily, or for a minimum period (Table 1).
